control_manifest.description: The same full-prefix implementation compared against itself.
control_manifest.exercises: Exact equality. The floor: any failure here is a bug in EvalLens itself.

control_manifest.description: Correct incremental cached decoding against a correct full-prefix pass.
control_manifest.exercises: Two genuinely different algorithms on the same weights. Floating-point accumulation order differs, so this must pass on the tolerance band rather than on equality.

control_manifest.description: Cached execution whose prefill covers the whole request.
control_manifest.exercises: The zero-decode-step boundary of the cached path.

control_manifest.description: A heavily left-padded row beside an unpadded one, both correct.
control_manifest.exercises: Correctly aligned padding transformations. If the position-ID convention were wrong, this control would fail instead of the padding mutants.

control_manifest.description: Several stateless rows of differing lengths in one batch.
control_manifest.exercises: Row independence in a ragged batch.

control_manifest.description: A three-request session with correct per-request cache reset.
control_manifest.exercises: Session state that is intentional within a request and cleared between them.

control_manifest.description: A correct implementation whose output projection is scaled by 1+1e-7 — a real difference, deliberately below the frozen tolerance.
control_manifest.exercises: The tolerance band itself. Without this, every control could pass by exact equality and the band would never be tested in the passing direction.

injected_faults_note: Every fault in this run was injected by EvalLens on purpose as test material for its own detector. None is a bug discovered in PyTorch or any other library.

mutant_manifest.description: The causal boundary is `k <= q + 1`, admitting exactly one future key.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Five distinct ascending tokens in one full-prefix row. Every position except the last gains one future key, so the leak shows at position 0 rather than only at the sequence end.

mutant_manifest.description: The final key column is always visible, regardless of query position.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Six distinct tokens so the last column carries information no earlier position should see; a repeated pattern could mask the leak by coincidence.

mutant_manifest.description: Padding columns are never masked, so pad embeddings enter attention.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Four left-padding columns before three real tokens. Padding must exist for a padding fault to be reachable at all; four columns make the contribution large enough to be unambiguous.

mutant_manifest.description: Only trailing padding is masked, so leading padding leaks into attention.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: A short left-padded row beside a long unpadded row. The second row sets the batch width so the first genuinely has leading padding to leak.

mutant_manifest.description: Each decode step embeds its token one position too early.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Prefill of one token leaves four decode steps, the maximum available for this length, so the offset applies to as many positions as possible.

mutant_manifest.description: Decode positions restart from zero instead of continuing the prefix.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: A prefill of three makes the restart offset three positions wide. With a prefill of one the restart would coincide with the correct position at the first decode step and the fault would be partly invisible.

mutant_manifest.description: A new key/value overwrites the most recent slot instead of extending.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Three decode steps after a prefill of two, so at least two writes land on an already-populated slot and permanently lose an earlier position.

mutant_manifest.description: Decode reads a cache view missing its oldest entry; the cache itself is intact.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: A prefill of two gives the dropped view something to drop from the first decode step onward. Prefill itself is untouched, which is what keeps this shape-valid and silent rather than a crash.

mutant_manifest.description: The cache is never cleared between requests of a session.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Two requests are the minimum that can expose a between-request reset, and the first is long enough that its residue meaningfully changes the second.

mutant_manifest.description: Only layer 0's cache is cleared between requests; deeper layers persist.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: A longer first request leaves more stale state in the layers that are not cleared. Partial resets are harder to see than none at all, because the first layer looks correct.
Epsilon enters every normalization in the model, so any valid case triggers it; a short row keeps the trigger cheap.

mutant_manifest.description: Normalization reduces over the token axis instead of the feature axis.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: More than one token is required for a token-axis reduction to differ from a feature-axis one; five tokens make the cross-token mixing unmistakable.

mutant_manifest.description: Scores are scaled by 1/d_head instead of 1/sqrt(d_head).
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Scaling only matters where a softmax has more than one candidate key, so the row is long enough for later positions to attend over several keys.

mutant_manifest.description: Scores are scaled by 1/sqrt(d_model) instead of 1/sqrt(d_head).
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: The classic confusion between model width and head width. Like the other scaling variant it needs several keys per softmax to be visible.

mutant_manifest.description: Layer 0's attention output for row 0 is broadcast across the batch.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Two rows with disjoint token values and equal lengths. Equal lengths remove padding as a confound, so a difference can only come from row mixing.

mutant_manifest.description: Attention values are rolled by one along the batch axis.
mutant_manifest.trigger_rationale: Three equal-length rows with disjoint tokens. Three rows make the roll a genuine permutation rather than a swap, so no row keeps its own values.
